cells.tense: The practice is being kept steady right now, by attention rather than by urgency.
cells.act: clear the ground of what came down
cells.ask: When a rule in your tradition asks to be protected, clear it out instead — take the piece that no longer holds and lay it aside, then leave that patch bare for a day. Rebuild nothing yet.
cells.core:
What you keep alive here is a small light made by repetition — tended in private, carried into what other people have handed down. When it's going well, the solitude doesn't cut you off, and the refinement isn't running on fear. You practice, and the people you practice with get what the practice makes of you.

Something false is going to fall — a rule, a habit, a concern about who's watching. The invitation isn't to hurry a replacement in. Take one inherited piece that no longer holds, lay it aside, and leave that patch bare for a day. Notice whether the practice still stands without it. It usually does, and what remains is more clearly yours to keep or to pass on.
cells.sheetLine: You keep one light lit, and it's enough.
cells.verb: keeping a practice alive until it becomes skill
cells.place: inside a tradition that carries what has been learned

cells.tense: The practice will be tightened again tomorrow before anyone has asked for it.
cells.act: surrender the outcome and keep the act
cells.ask: Name the result you keep measuring this practice against, then drop the score while the doing continues. Afterward, leave your hands still for one evening.
cells.core:
The refinement is running ahead of you now. You're preparing for a judgment the tradition didn't set, and the private hours have started feeling required rather than chosen. What was an offering has become a measuring stick held over every repetition.

Release here isn't defeat. Name the result you're gripping hardest — the level, the acknowledgment, the proof the time was spent well — and drop the score while the act itself continues. Then leave your hands still for one evening. The practice carries on without you standing over it, which is how it worked before. What's left when the score is gone is the part that was actually yours.
cells.sheetLine: You're refining past the point anyone asked for.
cells.verb: keeping a practice alive until it becomes skill
cells.place: inside a tradition that carries what has been learned

cells.tense: You are still standing at the doorway of a practice you once set out to carry.
cells.act: give back what is owed, and take what is yours
cells.ask: Find someone who carries this tradition and owes you nothing. Ask them for a lesson that is yours to receive, learn it, and hand something back in return. Make it even, then stop.
cells.core:
Practice here hasn't been sustained, and it wasn't for lack of wanting. You can feel the light that was meant to be kept, and nobody is tending it. That's where you're standing.

What returns you is proportion, not more effort. Learning moves by trading hands: find someone who carries this tradition and owes you nothing, ask for a lesson that is yours to receive, and hand something back in return. No debt kept, no score between you. Start with a single fair exchange, and let another come if you choose. The ground under the doorway starts to feel like ground you can walk on.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped carrying the practice, and the brake was real.
cells.verb: keeping a practice alive until it becomes skill
cells.place: inside a tradition that carries what has been learned

cells.tense: Skill keeps arriving in your hands without your having decided to build it.
cells.act: let the path show itself instead of forcing clarity
cells.ask: Take the thing you're already fluent in and follow where it's going — a step at a time, without planning the rest — and note what you find.
cells.core:
People come to you for what you're fluent in, and your account has you simply knowing it. You've absorbed a tradition so completely that the hours behind it went invisible, and you've started treating those hours as something you didn't have to give. What arrived without trying arrived somehow.

Try following instead of claiming. Take the thing you're already skilled at and follow where it's heading — one step, no plan for the rest — and note what you find. The point isn't to name the hours behind it. It's to see where the work wants to go, so the practice that made it becomes something you can keep, shape, or set down deliberately.
cells.sheetLine: You're already good at it, and you don't say you practiced.
cells.verb: keeping a practice alive until it becomes skill
cells.place: inside a tradition that carries what has been learned

attempts.check: The record gives the Too Little signature 'past experiences have made practice feel dangerous' — I can say that practice hasn't been sustained here, but not what past events caused it, who was there, or what was learned. The reader may object that solitude in this seat is exactly the point and that discipline has always been kept alone, so an ask that brings proportion with a teacher or people may read as a strange fit; if my read is wrong, the act still stands: making one fair trade of practice for acknowledgment, or taking back what is due for what they give to the culture, is useful regardless of the mechanism. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person is the easy symmetry of 'practice flows without force,' so I will not use it.
